A narrowly scoped runner integration packet and paired review were added; neither is an accepted fix.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN's new lightweight worktrees solve the asset-download problem, but the first independent review exposed another obstacle: the review launcher still requested a full checkout. The storage guard correctly refused the request before creating a claim. A follow-up workstream now targets the missing connection between the reviewer and the selective-checkout system.

sections.heading: A safety check did its job
sections.text: The new packet records a review attempt needing roughly 7.26 GB including reserve with only 2.28 GB available at that attempt. Rather than creating another stranded claim, the dispatcher rejected it. These are reported measurements from the attempt, not a live disk reading.

sections.heading: The missing link is in the review launcher
sections.text: The dispatcher already understands a checkout profile, but the paired-review runner did not forward one. The proposed fix must check that the smaller checkout contains every file needed to evaluate the implementation, including the actual changed files. A small checkout cannot become an excuse for incomplete review.

sections.heading: A new gate before Awakening
sections.text: New implementation and independent-review packets define the repair and its checks. GitHub workflow commits show packet handoffs, not proof that an agent is running or that the fix is landed. The original provisioning review still needs a genuine accepted verdict before protected recovery can be considered.

insights.title: A safe failure is progress, not completion
insights.explanation: The capacity preflight prevented a second stranded claim. That validates an important failure boundary while revealing that the reviewer still needs to adopt the new checkout mechanism.

insights.title: Review completeness is the real constraint
insights.explanation: The proposed minimal profile must cover the exact implementation diff and both packets' declared evidence. Otherwise a smaller reviewer worktree could silently omit the material needed for independent judgment.

The implementation is archived on main; independent review and authorization are still required before the protected Awakening claim can resume.

article.lead: A storage bottleneck that stranded Awakening development now has a code-level remedy. CUSTODIAN has landed an optional lightweight checkout that prepares only the assets a task needs, while preserving its ordinary full-checkout behavior. The fix is not yet clearance to restart the interrupted work: independent review remains outstanding.

sections.heading: Why the old checkout stalled
sections.text: CUSTODIAN's art-heavy repository uses Git Large File Storage (LFS). Preparing a new worktree could require several gigabytes of assets before the agent could begin. The archived task records an Awakening checkout that failed when storage ran out after its claim was already acquired.

sections.heading: A smaller, verifiable path
sections.text: The new profile lists exact required files and hydrates them from existing local LFS objects, checking expected sizes and hashes. Capacity is checked before acquiring a claim and again before checkout writes. The original full checkout remains the default, while a guarded recovery path targets the exact interrupted claim rather than creating another one.

sections.heading: A gate remains before gameplay resumes
sections.text: The implementation and its completion packet are on main, but the paired independent review is still marked ready. The review must challenge ownership, identity, storage, asset integrity and interrupted-checkout safeguards. Neither landing nor reported tests constitute accepted review or proof of clean host teardown.

insights.title: Storage pressure is now addressed before ownership changes
insights.explanation: The new preflight is intended to reject predictable capacity failures before creating a remote dispatch claim. That directly targets the failure mode that stranded the Awakening workstream, rather than merely shrinking asset downloads.

insights.title: The smaller checkout remains reproducible
insights.explanation: The published profile names exact files and LFS objects, and its local-only hydration checks identities. This makes a selective checkout auditable instead of treating missing art assets as an acceptable shortcut.

article.takeaway: The storage remedy has landed, but its safety claims still need independent acceptance before the protected Awakening recovery can proceed.
article.next_watch: Watch for a genuine independent PASS on the lightweight provisioning review, followed by separately authorized exact-claim recovery with trustworthy host evidence.

Either choice persists, the inscriptions remain readable, and a pale growth appears on later visits. Implementation validation is reported passing; independent review remains ready, not accepted.

article.lead: A small mystery in CUSTODIAN's Hub can now end with a deliberate choice. Once the Operator has examined all three inscriptions at the Sepulcher grave, two physical interactions become available: attest that the records conflict, or leave the matter unresolved. The choice is remembered, without rewriting the evidence.

sections.heading: A choice that respects the mystery
sections.text: Both outcomes are persistent and mutually exclusive. The original three readings stay available, so the player can revisit the clues without changing the record. The design avoids turning a disputed history into a forced revelation.

sections.heading: The world remembers quietly
sections.text: On a later visit, a pale growth appears beside the slab. It is a small environmental response rather than a new obstacle: the implementation adds no collision owner and leaves Contract preparation unchanged.

sections.heading: Landed code still needs independent eyes

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has moved an important review safeguard from a queued plan into the code on main. Before a workstream publishes changes, its finish workflow now checks whether synchronization merges have authentic lifecycle evidence. That closes a route by which a change could land only to fail later provenance review.

sections.heading: A checkpoint before publication
sections.text: The new guard examines merges along a workstream's source history, checking their ancestry, reconstructed tree and matching lifecycle records. Missing or inconsistent witnesses now block publication. Ordinary histories without synchronization merges remain compatible.

These results support the implementation, but a fresh independent review is still required. Existing protected historical reviews are not automatically forgiven by the new guard.

insights.title: The evidence check moved upstream
insights.explanation: Rejecting an unauthenticated merge before publication is more useful than discovering its missing history after a review is already stranded. This is a workflow reliability improvement, not a gameplay feature.

insights.title: The next bottleneck is independent acceptance

article.lead: A safety gap in CUSTODIAN's code-review pipeline now has a concrete repair plan. Two newly readied task packets propose checking the authenticity of synchronization history before changes can land, rather than discovering missing evidence only when independent review begins.

sections.heading: The problem sits between finishing and reviewing
sections.text: The current review verifier rejects a code history when it cannot authenticate a synchronization merge. The newly documented gap is earlier in the process: a workstream may publish its changes without proving that every earlier merge has the required lifecycle record.

sections.heading: The proposed fix has its own independent test
sections.text: The implementation packet calls for a fail-closed check before publication, with real-Git regression tests. A separate review packet must then examine both the new guard and the complete current validator. Neither packet being ready establishes that an agent is running.

insights.title: Preventing bad evidence is stronger than repairing it afterward
insights.explanation: The proposed change moves a provenance check earlier, where it can stop an unverifiable workstream before landing. That could reduce the accumulation of historical review-recovery cases.

insights.title: Recertification is not retroactive forgiveness
insights.explanation: Even a successful new review would not automatically accept or close older protected review runs. Their original evidence and separate authorization requirements remain intact.

article.takeaway: The guard is queued, not landed; its independent acceptance remains a future gate.
article.next_watch: An implementation commit and real-Git validation evidence, followed by a genuine independent review receipt.

sections.heading: Why historical rules matter
sections.text: A review of older work must establish which tests and coverage rules were in force at the exact source revision. The correction authenticates a tightly scoped test-definition change and applies the same pinned rules to failed reports, successful reports and final closeout.

insights.title: Consistency across the whole review lifecycle

insights.title: Test runtime is a separate maintenance concern
